items.text: Why ___ your neighbor usually leave for work before six, even on cold winter mornings?

ok.de: Gewohnheit in der Frage: does + Grundform (did ist auch richtig: Gewohnheit in der Vergangenheit). Zu neighbor (Singular) passt does.
ok.en: A habit in a question takes does + base form (did is also correct: a habit in the past). The singular neighbor goes with does.

wrong.de: is braucht -ing (leaving), hier steht aber die Grundform leave.
wrong.en: is needs -ing (leaving), but the sentence has the base form leave.

wrong.de: do passt zu I, you, we, they, nicht zu neighbor (Singular).
wrong.en: do goes with I, you, we, they, not with the singular neighbor.

wrong.de: will meint die Zukunft, usually beschreibt aber eine Gewohnheit.
wrong.en: will means the future, but usually describes a habit.

items.lead: At the moment our landlord is replacing all the old windows in the building.
items.after: all the old windows in the building.

ok.de: Teil 1: is currently, denn die Lage gilt gerade jetzt. Teil 2: replacing, die -ing-Form zeigt, dass es im Moment läuft.
ok.en: Part 1: is currently, because the situation applies right now. Part 2: replacing, the -ing form shows it is in progress at the moment.

wrong.de: Nach is steht die -ing-Form: replacing. Die Grundform replace passt nicht.
wrong.en: After is comes the -ing form: replacing. The base form replace does not fit.

items.text: I think the new pricing model is too complicated for most of our small customers, so we should simplify it.

ok.de: Kein Fehler: think im Sinn von „meinen“ ist ein Zustandsverb und steht ohne -ing. Mit -ing hieße es „nachdenken“.
ok.en: No mistake: think meaning “to hold an opinion” is a state verb and takes no -ing. With -ing it would mean “to consider”.

wrong.de: Bei „meinen“ braucht think keine -ing-Form. I am thinking wäre hier falsch.
wrong.en: Meaning “to hold an opinion”, think needs no -ing form. I am thinking would be wrong here.

wrong.de: Der Satz ist richtig: An dieser Stelle steckt kein Fehler.
wrong.en: The sentence is correct: there is no mistake at this spot.

items.text: Our new colleague ___ always forgetting to attach the files, and I have to remind him every single time.

ok.de: always + -ing drückt Ärger über Wiederholung aus: is always forgetting. is steht vor always.
ok.en: always + -ing expresses annoyance at repetition: is always forgetting. is comes before always.

wrong.de: has + forgetting gibt es nicht; has braucht das Partizip forgotten.
wrong.en: has + forgetting does not exist; has needs the participle forgotten.

wrong.de: does braucht die Grundform, hier steht aber forgetting.
wrong.en: does needs the base form, but forgetting follows here.

wrong.de: was ist Vergangenheit, der Satz meint aber die Gegenwart.
wrong.en: was is past, but the sentence is about the present.

items.lead: It is very unusual for our CEO to work from home on Fridays.

ok.de: Teil 1: hardly ever steht vor dem Verb. Teil 2: works, mit -s bei he/she/it, denn es ist eine Gewohnheit.
ok.en: Part 1: hardly ever goes before the verb. Part 2: works, with -s for he/she/it, because it is a habit.

wrong.de: Bei he/she/it braucht das Present Simple ein -s: works.
wrong.en: With he/she/it the present simple needs an -s: works.

wrong.de: Eine Gewohnheit steht im Present Simple, nicht in der -ing-Form.
wrong.en: A habit takes the present simple, not the -ing form.

items.text: We are needing the signed contract by Friday, otherwise the project cannot start on time.

ok.de: need ist ein Zustandsverb und hat keine -ing-Form: We need … Auch „gerade jetzt“ ändert daran nichts.
ok.en: need is a state verb and has no -ing form: We need … Even “right now” does not change that.

wrong.de: are braucht -ing oder ein Adjektiv; need ist die Grundform.
wrong.en: are needs -ing or an adjective; need is the base form.

wrong.de: needs passt zu he/she/it, nicht zu we.
wrong.en: needs goes with he/she/it, not with we.

wrong.de: Der Fehler steckt bei „are needing“, nicht hier.
wrong.en: The mistake is at “are needing”, not here.

wrong.de: Doch, hier steckt ein Fehler: „are needing“ ist falsch.
wrong.en: There is a mistake: “are needing” is wrong.

items.text: My manager ___ not believe in long meetings, so ours never last more than thirty minutes.

ok.de: believe ist ein Zustandsverb: Present Simple mit does not, nie is believing.
ok.en: believe is a state verb: present simple with does not, never is believing.

wrong.de: is not believe gibt es nicht; believe hat kein -ing.
wrong.en: is not believe does not exist; believe takes no -ing form.

wrong.de: has braucht ein Partizip (believed), nicht die Grundform.
wrong.en: has needs a participle (believed), not the base form.

wrong.de: manager ist Singular: do passt zu I, you, we, they.
wrong.en: manager is singular: do goes with I, you, we, they.

items.lead: Few colleagues drink the new coffee in our kitchen because its flavor is rather bitter.
items.before: Few colleagues drink the new coffee in our kitchen because it

ok.de: Teil 1: tastes, denn „schmecken“ ist hier ein Zustandsverb ohne -ing. Teil 2: ein Adjektiv (rather bitter) beschreibt den Geschmack.
ok.en: Part 1: tastes, because “to taste” is a state verb here, without -ing. Part 2: an adjective (rather bitter) describes the flavor.

wrong.de: Nach tastes steht ein Adjektiv, kein Adverb: bitter, nicht bitterly.
wrong.en: After tastes comes an adjective, not an adverb: bitter, not bitterly.

items.text: My cousin ___ not know about the wedding until last Saturday, so she could not book a train in time.

ok.de: Mit last Saturday steht das Past Simple: did not + Grundform.
ok.en: With last Saturday the past simple is used: did not + base form.

wrong.de: has braucht das Partizip (known); last Saturday ist ein abgeschlossener Zeitpunkt.
wrong.en: has needs the participle (known); last Saturday is a finished point in time.

wrong.de: does steht in der Gegenwart; last Saturday liegt in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: does is present tense; last Saturday is in the past.

wrong.de: is not know gibt es nicht; vor der Grundform steht did.
wrong.en: is not know does not exist; the base form needs did.

items.lead: Our company moved into this building at the start of 2020 and is still based here.

ok.de: Teil 1: has been, weil die Lage bis heute dauert. Teil 2: since nennt den Startpunkt (Beginn von 2020).
ok.en: Part 1: has been, because the situation lasts until today. Part 2: since names the starting point (the start of 2020).

wrong.de: Das Past Simple endet in der Vergangenheit; „seit“ bis heute braucht has been.
wrong.en: The past simple ends in the past; “since” up to now needs has been.

wrong.de: Deutsch sagt „ist seit … hier“ im Präsens. Englisch braucht has been.
wrong.en: German uses the present for “ist seit … hier”. English needs has been.

items.text: This is the best onboarding workshop that I never attended in my five years at this company.

ok.de: Nach einem Superlativ steht ever: „der Beste, den ich je besucht habe“ = have ever attended (Present Perfect, Erfahrung bis heute).
ok.en: After a superlative comes ever: “the best I have ever attended” = have ever attended (present perfect, experience up to now).

wrong.de: Nach einem Superlativ steht ever, nicht never: „der Beste, den ich nie besuchte“ ergibt keinen Sinn.
wrong.en: After a superlative comes ever, not never: “the best I have never attended” makes no sense.

wrong.de: Nach did steht die Grundform: did … attend, nicht attended.
wrong.en: After did comes the base form: did … attend, not attended.

wrong.de: Der Fehler steckt bei „never attended“, nicht hier.
wrong.en: The mistake is at “never attended”, not here.

wrong.de: Doch, hier steckt ein Fehler: „never attended“ ist falsch.
wrong.en: There is a mistake: “never attended” is wrong.

items.text: I ___ not received the parcel with the shelf yet, so I cannot start building the bedroom furniture.

ok.de: yet verlangt das Present Perfect: have not received. Das Ergebnis gilt jetzt noch.
ok.en: yet calls for the present perfect: have not received. The result still applies now.

wrong.de: am not received gibt es nicht; vor dem Partizip received steht have.
wrong.en: am not received does not exist; the participle received needs have.

wrong.de: was not received wäre Passiv („wurde nicht empfangen“) und passt nicht zu I.
wrong.en: was not received would be passive and does not fit I.

wrong.de: will braucht die Grundform (receive), nicht received.
wrong.en: will needs the base form (receive), not received.

items.lead: At what exact time did the failure of the system happen?

ok.de: Teil 1: when did, denn when nennt einen abgeschlossenen Zeitpunkt. Teil 2: the system fail, nach did steht die Grundform.
ok.en: Part 1: when did, because when names a finished point in time. Part 2: the system fail, the base form follows did.

wrong.de: Mit when fragst du nach einem Zeitpunkt, deshalb steht das Past Simple: did … fail.
wrong.en: With when you ask for a point in time, so the past simple is used: did … fail.

items.text: We are partners with the Hamburg team since 2019 and have never had a serious conflict.

ok.de: since 2019 meint „bis heute“: Das braucht das Present Perfect, also have been partners. Deutsch nutzt hier das Präsens.
ok.en: since 2019 means “up to today”: that needs the present perfect, so have been partners. German uses the present here.

wrong.de: were passt zu einem Ende in der Vergangenheit; since 2019 reicht aber bis heute.
wrong.en: were fits an end in the past, but since 2019 reaches up to today.

wrong.de: are being partners ist keine übliche Form; Zustände mit since stehen im Present Perfect.
wrong.en: are being partners is not a normal form; states with since use the present perfect.

wrong.de: Der Fehler steckt bei „are partners“, nicht hier.
wrong.en: The mistake is at “are partners”, not here.

wrong.de: Doch, hier steckt ein Fehler: „are partners“ ist falsch.
wrong.en: There is a mistake: “are partners” is wrong.

items.text: We have been using this document management system ___ more than six years without any major problems.

ok.de: for + Zeitspanne (six years) beantwortet „wie lange“. Dazu passt have been using.
ok.en: for + a length of time (six years) answers “how long”. have been using fits it.

wrong.de: since nennt einen Startpunkt (since 2019), nicht eine Dauer wie six years.
wrong.en: since names a starting point (since 2019), not a length like six years.

wrong.de: during steht vor einer Phase (during the project), nicht vor einer Dauer.
wrong.en: during goes before a phase (during the project), not before a length of time.

wrong.de: from braucht ein Gegenstück (from … to …); hier fehlt der Anfangspunkt.
wrong.en: from needs a counterpart (from … to …); there is no starting point here.

items.lead: Nobody has complained about the new release up to now.

ok.de: Teil 1: have been, denn so far blickt bis jetzt. Teil 2: no complaints so far, so far = bis jetzt.
ok.en: Part 1: have been, because so far looks up to now. Part 2: no complaints so far, so far = up to now.

wrong.de: so far verlangt das Present Perfect: have been, nicht were.
wrong.en: so far calls for the present perfect: have been, not were.

items.text: Our neighbors ___ been renovating their kitchen since early April, and the noise is still not over.

ok.de: Eine Tätigkeit seit April bis heute: have been renovating (Present Perfect Continuous).
ok.en: An activity from April up to today: have been renovating (present perfect continuous).

wrong.de: are been gibt es nicht; vor been steht have.
wrong.en: are been does not exist; been needs have.

wrong.de: did braucht die Grundform (renovate), nicht been renovating.
wrong.en: did needs the base form (renovate), not been renovating.

wrong.de: were been ist falsch; die Dauer bis jetzt braucht have been.
wrong.en: were been is wrong; duration up to now needs have been.

items.lead: Our call with the client started twenty minutes ago and is still going.

ok.de: Teil 1: have been talking, die Tätigkeit läuft noch. Teil 2: for + Dauer (twenty minutes).
ok.en: Part 1: have been talking, the activity is still going on. Part 2: for + length of time (twenty minutes).

wrong.de: Deutsch sagt „wir sprechen seit 20 Minuten“ im Präsens. Englisch braucht have been talking.
wrong.en: German says “wir sprechen seit 20 Minuten” in the present. English needs have been talking.

items.text: The auditors have been reviewing our travel expense reports for most of the afternoon now.

ok.de: Kein Fehler: have been + -ing (reviewing) beschreibt eine Tätigkeit, die bis jetzt dauert.
ok.en: No mistake: have been + -ing (reviewing) describes an activity that has lasted until now.

wrong.de: Nach have been steht die -ing-Form. reviewing ist genau richtig.
wrong.en: After have been comes the -ing form. reviewing is exactly right.

wrong.de: Der Satz ist richtig: An dieser Stelle steckt kein Fehler.
wrong.en: The sentence is correct: there is no mistake at this spot.

items.text: You look exhausted: ___ you been sleeping badly lately, or is the new project too much?

ok.de: lately blickt auf eine Spur in der Gegenwart: have you been sleeping. Die Frage fragt nach der letzten Zeit.
ok.en: lately looks at a trace in the present: have you been sleeping. The question is about recent weeks.

wrong.de: did braucht die Grundform (sleep); mit been sleeping muss have stehen.
wrong.en: did needs the base form (sleep); been sleeping needs have.

wrong.de: are you been gibt es nicht; vor been steht have.
wrong.en: are you been does not exist; been needs have.

wrong.de: do braucht die Grundform; been sleeping verlangt have.
wrong.en: do needs the base form; been sleeping calls for have.

items.lead: I first met Dana in 2018.

ok.de: Teil 1: have known, ein Zustandsverb steht im einfachen Present Perfect. Teil 2: Dana since, since nennt den Startpunkt.
ok.en: Part 1: have known, a state verb uses the simple present perfect. Part 2: Dana since, since names the starting point.

wrong.de: Deutsch sagt „ich kenne sie seit …“ im Präsens. Englisch braucht have known.
wrong.en: German says “ich kenne sie seit …” in the present. English needs have known.

wrong.de: know ist ein Zustandsverb und hat keine -ing-Form: have known.
wrong.en: know is a state verb and has no -ing form: have known.

items.text: The vendor has been promising a fix since three weeks, but nothing has changed so far.

ok.de: for nennt eine Dauer (three weeks), since einen Startpunkt (since March). Deutsch „seit“ deckt beides ab.
ok.en: for names a length (three weeks), since a starting point (since March). German “seit” covers both.

wrong.de: from braucht ein Gegenstück (from … to …) und passt nicht zu has been promising.
wrong.en: from needs a counterpart (from … to …) and does not fit has been promising.

wrong.de: during steht vor einer Phase (during the call), nicht vor einer Dauer.
wrong.en: during goes before a phase (during the call), not before a length of time.

wrong.de: Der Fehler steckt bei „since three weeks“, nicht hier.
wrong.en: The mistake is at “since three weeks”, not here.

wrong.de: Doch, hier steckt ein Fehler: „since three weeks“ ist falsch.
wrong.en: There is a mistake: “since three weeks” is wrong.

items.text: Our new colleague ___ written three reports since Monday, which is more than the whole team managed last week.

ok.de: Ein Ergebnis zählt (three reports): einfaches Present Perfect, has written. Die -ing-Form betont die Tätigkeit.
ok.en: A result is counted (three reports): simple present perfect, has written. The -ing form stresses the activity.

wrong.de: is written ist Passiv; hier schreibt die Kollegin selbst.
wrong.en: is written is passive, but the colleague does the writing herself.

wrong.de: did braucht die Grundform (write), nicht written.
wrong.en: did needs the base form (write), not written.

wrong.de: was written wäre Passiv in der Vergangenheit; since Monday verlangt das Present Perfect.
wrong.en: was written would be a past passive; since Monday calls for the present perfect.

items.lead: Dana started negotiating the contract in May and is still negotiating it.

ok.de: Teil 1: has been, weil es seit Mai bis jetzt läuft. Teil 2: negotiating, die -ing-Form zeigt die laufende Tätigkeit.
ok.en: Part 1: has been, because it has run from May until now. Part 2: negotiating, the -ing form shows the ongoing activity.

wrong.de: Mit -ed wäre es Passiv („wurde verhandelt“). Dana verhandelt selbst, also -ing.
wrong.en: With -ed it would be passive (“was negotiated”). Dana negotiates herself, so -ing.

items.text: By the time we reached the cinema, the film ___ already started, so we missed the opening scene.

ok.de: Das Frühere vor einem Zeitpunkt in der Vergangenheit: had + Partizip (had already started).
ok.en: What happened earlier than a past point in time: had + participle (had already started).

wrong.de: has gehört zum Present Perfect; der Satz erzählt aber in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: has belongs to the present perfect, but the sentence tells a story in the past.

wrong.de: was already started klänge wie Passiv; der Film begann von selbst.
wrong.en: was already started would sound passive; the film started by itself.

wrong.de: did braucht die Grundform (start), nicht started.
wrong.en: did needs the base form (start), not started.

items.lead: On Monday my manager promised to send me the report the next day.

ok.de: Teil 1: said she would, denn die Aussage lag in der Vergangenheit, deshalb rückt will zu would. Teil 2: send me, nach would folgt die Grundform.
ok.en: Part 1: said she would, because the statement was in the past, so will moves back to would. Part 2: send me, the base form follows would.

wrong.de: In der berichteten Rede rückt will eine Stufe zurück: would.
wrong.en: In reported speech will moves one step back: would.

items.text: When the inspector arrived at nine, we were waiting for him since seven-thirty.

ok.de: Eine Dauer bis zu einem Zeitpunkt in der Vergangenheit braucht had been + -ing: had been waiting since seven-thirty.
ok.en: A length of time up to a point in the past needs had been + -ing: had been waiting since seven-thirty.

wrong.de: have been waiting gehört in die Gegenwart; die Erzählung steht aber in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: have been waiting belongs to the present, but the story is told in the past.

wrong.de: waited zeigt nicht, dass das Warten bis neun andauerte; mit since braucht es had (been).
wrong.en: waited does not show that the waiting lasted until nine; with since it needs had (been).

wrong.de: Der Fehler steckt bei „were waiting“, nicht hier.
wrong.en: The mistake is at “were waiting”, not here.

wrong.de: Doch, hier steckt ein Fehler: „were waiting“ ist falsch.
wrong.en: There is a mistake: “were waiting” is wrong.

items.text: It was the first time I ___ ever traveled alone, and I was a little nervous at the airport.

ok.de: Nach It was the first time steht das Past Perfect: I had ever traveled.
ok.en: After It was the first time the past perfect follows: I had ever traveled.

wrong.de: have passt zur Gegenwart; der Satz erzählt aber in der Vergangenheit (was).
wrong.en: have fits the present, but the sentence is told in the past (was).

wrong.de: was braucht -ing oder ein Adjektiv; traveled ist weder noch.
wrong.en: was needs -ing or an adjective; traveled is neither.

wrong.de: did braucht die Grundform (travel), nicht traveled.
wrong.en: did needs the base form (travel), not traveled.

items.lead: We had barely started the demo when the projector stopped working.
items.after: the demo than the projector stopped working.

ok.de: Teil 1: sooner had, nach No sooner steht das Hilfsverb. Teil 2: we started, danach folgt das Subjekt mit dem Partizip.
ok.en: Part 1: sooner had, the auxiliary follows No sooner. Part 2: we started, the subject and participle come next.

wrong.de: Nach No sooner steht had vor dem Subjekt: had we started.
wrong.en: After No sooner, had comes before the subject: had we started.

items.text: By the time the guests arrived, we had already cleaned the apartment and cooked dinner.

ok.de: Kein Fehler: had already cleaned zeigt, dass das Putzen vor der Ankunft der Gäste fertig war.
ok.en: No mistake: had already cleaned shows that the cleaning was finished before the guests arrived.

wrong.de: had + Partizip ist hier richtig: Es war schon vor der Ankunft passiert.
wrong.en: had + participle is right here: it had already happened before the arrival.

wrong.de: Der Satz ist richtig: An dieser Stelle steckt kein Fehler.
wrong.en: The sentence is correct: there is no mistake at this spot.

items.text: My teacher asked whether we ___ already finished the homework for the weekend before the lesson began.

ok.de: Berichtete Frage in der Vergangenheit: had + Partizip (had already finished) für das Frühere.
ok.en: A reported question in the past: had + participle (had already finished) for the earlier action.

wrong.de: did braucht die Grundform (finish), nicht finished.
wrong.en: did needs the base form (finish), not finished.

wrong.de: would braucht die Grundform (finish), nicht finished.
wrong.en: would needs the base form (finish), not finished.

wrong.de: were finished + Objekt geht nicht; die Handlung braucht had finished.
wrong.en: were finished plus an object does not work; the action needs had finished.

items.lead: Our team began testing the update at seven, and the client arrived at nine.

ok.de: Teil 1: had been, denn die Dauer endet vor dem Zeitpunkt in der Vergangenheit. Teil 2: testing, die -ing-Form zeigt die Tätigkeit.
ok.en: Part 1: had been, because the length of time ends before a point in the past. Part 2: testing, the -ing form shows the activity.

wrong.de: Mit -ed wäre es Passiv („wurde getestet“). Das Team testet selbst, also -ing.
wrong.en: With -ed it would be passive (“was tested”). The team does the testing, so -ing.

items.text: There ___ to be a small bakery on our street, but it closed years ago.

ok.de: used to + Grundform beschreibt einen früheren Zustand, den es heute nicht mehr gibt.
ok.en: used to + base form describes an earlier state that no longer exists today.

wrong.de: In der bejahten Aussage heißt es used to, mit -d.
wrong.en: In a positive statement it is used to, with a -d.

wrong.de: would to gibt es nicht; und would passt nicht zu There ... to be.
wrong.en: would to does not exist; and would does not fit There ... to be.

wrong.de: am to be passt nicht zu There und nicht zur Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: am to be fits neither There nor the past.

items.lead: Working under constant time pressure no longer feels strange to me.

ok.de: Teil 1: am used to, so sagst du „ich bin es gewohnt“. Teil 2: working, nach used to steht hier die -ing-Form, weil to eine Präposition ist.
ok.en: Part 1: am used to, that is how you say “I am accustomed to it”. Part 2: working, the -ing form follows because to is a preposition here.

wrong.de: Nach be used to folgt die -ing-Form: working.
wrong.en: After be used to the -ing form follows: working.

wrong.de: used to + Grundform meint früher; be used to + -ing meint gewohnt sein.
wrong.en: used to + base form means formerly; be used to + -ing means being accustomed.

items.text: We didn't used to have a dishwasher, so we washed everything by hand after dinner.

ok.de: Nach didn’t steht die Grundform: didn’t use to. Das -d von used verschwindet, weil didn’t schon die Vergangenheit trägt.
ok.en: After didn’t the base form follows: didn’t use to. The -d of used disappears, because didn’t already carries the past.

wrong.de: don’t use ist Gegenwart; der Satz erzählt aber von früher (washed).
wrong.en: don’t use is present tense, but the sentence tells about the past (washed).

wrong.de: weren’t braucht ein Partizip oder -ing, nicht use.
wrong.en: weren’t needs a participle or -ing, not use.

wrong.de: Der Fehler steckt bei „didn't used“, nicht hier.
wrong.en: The mistake is at “didn't used”, not here.

wrong.de: Doch, hier steckt ein Fehler: „didn't used“ ist falsch.
wrong.en: There is a mistake: “didn't used” is wrong.

items.text: It took the new team a few months to get used ___ the strict approval process.

ok.de: get used to + Nomen beschreibt den Weg zum Gewohntsein: get used to the process.
ok.en: get used to + noun describes becoming accustomed: get used to the process.

wrong.de: get used with gibt es nicht; die feste Verbindung ist get used to.
wrong.en: get used with does not exist; the fixed combination is get used to.

wrong.de: get used for hieße „benutzt werden für“ und ergibt hier keinen Sinn.
wrong.en: get used for would mean “be used for” and makes no sense here.

wrong.de: at passt nicht zu get used; die Verbindung braucht to.
wrong.en: at does not go with get used; the combination needs to.

items.lead: Every summer in my childhood, we frequently drove to the lake on weekends.
items.before: Every summer in my childhood, we

ok.de: Teil 1: would often, so erzählst du wiederholte Handlungen in der Vergangenheit. Teil 2: drive, nach would steht die Grundform.
ok.en: Part 1: would often, that is how you tell repeated actions in the past. Part 2: drive, the base form follows would.

wrong.de: Bei would steht das Häufigkeitswort danach: would often drive.
wrong.en: With would the frequency word comes after it: would often drive.

items.text: After years in sales, I'm used to deal with difficult customers on a daily basis.

ok.de: be used to + -ing: I’m used to dealing. Hier ist to eine Präposition, deshalb folgt die -ing-Form.
ok.en: be used to + -ing: I’m used to dealing. Here to is a preposition, so the -ing form follows.

wrong.de: use to deal gibt es nicht in dieser Form; be used to braucht used mit -d und -ing.
wrong.en: use to deal does not exist in this form; be used to needs used with -d and -ing.

wrong.de: used dealing lässt to weg: be used to + -ing.
wrong.en: used dealing leaves out to: be used to + -ing.

wrong.de: Der Fehler steckt bei „used to deal“, nicht hier.
wrong.en: The mistake is at “used to deal”, not here.

wrong.de: Doch, hier steckt ein Fehler: „used to deal“ ist falsch.
wrong.en: There is a mistake: “used to deal” is wrong.

items.text: Before the pandemic started, ___ you use to go to the gym at least three times a week?

ok.de: Frage über früher: did + Subjekt + use to + Grundform; das -d von used entfällt.
ok.en: A question about the past: did + subject + use to + base form; the -d of used drops.

wrong.de: do you use to passt nicht zu Before the pandemic started (Vergangenheit).
wrong.en: do you use to does not fit Before the pandemic started (past).

wrong.de: were you use to gibt es nicht; die Frage braucht did.
wrong.en: were you use to does not exist; the question needs did.

wrong.de: have you use to gibt es nicht; die Frage braucht did.
wrong.en: have you use to does not exist; the question needs did.

items.lead: Years ago our company kept all its records in paper files, but now everything is digital.

items.before: The migration would be finished by now

ok.de: Teil 1: had we, die Umstellung ersetzt if: Had we hired … Teil 2: hired another developer, danach folgt das Partizip.
ok.en: Part 1: had we, the inversion replaces if: Had we hired … Part 2: hired another developer, the participle follows.

wrong.de: Nach had we steht das Partizip: hired.
wrong.en: The participle follows had we: hired.

items.text: I was wondering ___ you could confirm the venue and the catering for next Thursday.

ok.de: I was wondering if … macht die Bitte weich: if oder whether leitet die indirekte Frage ein.
ok.en: I was wondering if … makes the request soft: if or whether introduces the indirect question.

wrong.de: Nach I was wondering folgt if oder whether, keine Frageform mit could.
wrong.en: I was wondering is followed by if or whether, not a question form with could.

wrong.de: that passt nicht, weil es eine Frage und keine Aussage ist.
wrong.en: that does not fit, because this is a question and not a statement.

wrong.de: do passt nicht; die indirekte Frage braucht if oder whether.
wrong.en: do does not fit; the indirect question needs if or whether.

items.lead: Please resend the invoice with the correct VAT number.
items.after: resend the invoice with the correct VAT number?

ok.de: Teil 1: would it be, die Frageform macht die Bitte höflich. Teil 2: possible to, danach steht die Grundform.
ok.en: Part 1: would it be, the question form makes the request polite. Part 2: possible to, the base form follows.

wrong.de: Nach possible steht to + Grundform, kein that-Satz.
wrong.en: To + base form follows possible, not a that clause.

items.text: We were hoping to getting your feedback on the draft before the end of the week.

ok.de: Nach hoping folgt to + Grundform: hoping to get. Die -ing-Form passt hier nicht.
ok.en: To + base form follows hoping: hoping to get. The -ing form does not fit here.

wrong.de: getting allein lässt to weg; hope verlangt to + Grundform.
wrong.en: getting alone leaves out to; hope requires to + base form.

wrong.de: for getting passt nicht zu hope; hier folgt to + Grundform.
wrong.en: for getting does not fit hope; to + base form follows here.

wrong.de: Der Fehler steckt bei „to getting“, nicht hier.
wrong.en: The mistake is at “to getting”, not here.

wrong.de: Doch, hier steckt ein Fehler: „to getting“ ist falsch.
wrong.en: There is a mistake: “to getting” is wrong.

items.text: Delivering by Friday would be a bit ___ a stretch for our team, to be honest.

ok.de: a bit of a stretch ist eine höfliche Untertreibung für einen echten Einwand.
ok.en: a bit of a stretch is a polite understatement for a real objection.

wrong.de: a bit from a stretch gibt es nicht; die Wendung ist a bit of a.
wrong.en: a bit from a stretch does not exist; the phrase is a bit of a.

wrong.de: than steht nach einem Komparativ, nicht nach a bit.
wrong.en: than follows a comparative, not a bit.

wrong.de: a bit for a stretch ist keine feste Wendung.
wrong.en: a bit for a stretch is not a fixed phrase.

items.lead: Please send me the agenda for the meeting before Friday.
items.after: me the agenda for the meeting before Friday.

ok.de: Teil 1: whether you, die indirekte Frage hat normale Wortstellung. Teil 2: could send, could macht die Bitte höflich.
ok.en: Part 1: whether you, the indirect question has normal word order. Part 2: could send, could makes the request polite.

wrong.de: Nach whether steht die normale Wortstellung: you could send.
wrong.en: Normal word order follows whether: you could send.

items.text: Would it be possible to move our call to Thursday afternoon, if that suits your calendar?

ok.de: Kein Fehler: Would it be possible to … + Grundform ist die höfliche Standardfrage.
ok.en: No mistake: Would it be possible to … + base form is the polite standard question.

wrong.de: possible to move ist hier richtig; nach possible folgt to + Grundform.
wrong.en: possible to move is right here; to + base form follows possible.

wrong.de: Der Satz ist richtig: An dieser Stelle steckt kein Fehler.
wrong.en: The sentence is correct: there is no mistake at this spot.

items.text: We were hoping you ___ be able to share the draft with us before the end of the week.

ok.de: We were hoping you would … drückt einen höflichen Wunsch aus; would rückt die Bitte in die Ferne (might ist auch möglich).
ok.en: We were hoping you would … expresses a polite wish; would puts distance on the request (might is also possible).

wrong.de: is be able gibt es nicht; nach were hoping steht would.
wrong.en: is be able does not exist; would follows were hoping.

wrong.de: can be able ist doppelt; außerdem fehlt die Zeitenfolge nach were hoping.
wrong.en: can be able is doubled; also the tense sequence after were hoping is missing.

wrong.de: do be able gibt es nicht; nach were hoping steht would.
wrong.en: do be able does not exist; would follows were hoping.

items.lead: The new deadline is a serious problem for our team.

ok.de: Teil 1: a bit macht die Aussage milder. Teil 2: of a challenge, die feste Wendung heißt a bit of a …
ok.en: Part 1: a bit makes the statement milder. Part 2: of a challenge, the fixed phrase is a bit of a …

wrong.de: Nach a bit steht of: a bit of a challenge.
wrong.en: Of follows a bit: a bit of a challenge.

items.lead: The new release is scheduled to go live at the end of May.

ok.de: Teil 1: is due, so sagst du „ist für … vorgesehen“. Teil 2: to go live, danach steht to und die Grundform.
ok.en: Part 1: is due, that is how you say “is scheduled for”. Part 2: to go live, to and the base form follow.

wrong.de: Nach due steht to + Grundform: due to go live.
wrong.en: To + base form follows due: due to go live.

items.lead: The conference is planned to start on Monday morning.

ok.de: Teil 1: is set, so sagst du „ist angesetzt“. Teil 2: to start, danach steht to und die Grundform.
ok.en: Part 1: is set, that is how you say “is scheduled”. Part 2: to start, to and the base form follow.

wrong.de: Nach set steht to + Grundform: set to start.
wrong.en: To + base form follows set: set to start.

items.lead: We will finish the documents before the auditors arrive on Monday.
items.before: We will have finished the documents
traps: by the time auditors will arrive

ok.de: Teil 1: by the time heißt „spätestens bis“. Teil 2: the auditors arrive, danach steht die Gegenwart.
ok.en: Part 1: by the time means “no later than”. Part 2: the auditors arrive, the present follows.

wrong.de: Nach by the time steht die Gegenwart, kein will: arrive.
wrong.en: The present follows by the time, no will: arrive.

items.lead: The vendor's team will complete the migration no later than March 31.
traps: will have complete the migration by

ok.de: Das Future Perfect (will have completed) betont „bis dahin fertig“; will complete ist auch richtig. by nennt die Frist.
ok.en: The future perfect (will have completed) stresses “finished by then”; will complete is also correct. by names the deadline.

wrong.de: Nach will have steht das Partizip: completed.
wrong.en: The participle follows will have: completed.

items.lead: We will accept the terms only if the client signs by Friday.
traps: provided that the client will sign

ok.de: Teil 1: provided that, so sagst du „unter der Bedingung, dass“. Teil 2: the client signs, danach steht die Gegenwart, kein will.
ok.en: Part 1: provided that, that is how you say “on condition that”. Part 2: the client signs, the present follows, no will.

wrong.de: Nach provided that steht wie nach if das Present Simple, kein will.
wrong.en: After provided that the present simple is used, as after if, no will.

items.lead: I am sorry that I did not listen to your advice.

ok.de: Teil 1: if only, so beginnt ein starker Wunsch. Teil 2: I had listened, für Vergangenes steht had + Partizip.
ok.en: Part 1: if only, that is how a strong wish begins. Part 2: I had listened, the past takes had + participle.

wrong.de: If only + had + Partizip drückt Bedauern über Vergangenes aus, nicht would.
wrong.en: If only + had + participle expresses regret about the past, not would.

items.lead: I prefer not to discuss the budget on the phone.

ok.de: Teil 1: would rather, so sagst du „ich möchte lieber“. Teil 2: not discuss, danach steht die Grundform ohne to.
ok.en: Part 1: would rather, that is how you say “I would prefer to”. Part 2: not discuss, the base form without to follows.

wrong.de: Nach would rather steht die Grundform ohne to.
wrong.en: The base form without to follows would rather.
